- **DiBud (Discrete Budgeted):** Jederzeit abbrechbare Streaming-Fusion unter Zeit-

public_items.name: AdaptiveConformalCalibrator
doc: Adaptive Conformal Calibrator for quantile-based online threshold estimation under covariate shift.
Implements online stochastic gradient updates on the weighted pinball loss for target coverage
level $1 - \alpha$. When a non-conformity score exceeds the current threshold ($S_t > \hat{q}_t$),
the threshold increases by $\gamma \cdot w_t \cdot (1 - \alpha)$. Otherwise, it decreases by
$\gamma \cdot w_t \cdot \alpha$.
Adaptiver konformer Kalibrierer für Online-Schwellenwerte unter Covariate Shift.

methods.name: fuse
methods.signature: pub fn fuse( &self, result_sets: Vec<(String, Vec<SearchResult>, f32)>, max_results: usize, ) -> Result<Vec<SearchResult>, RankError>
doc: Fuses multi-signal search results using community-aware RRF.
Candidates are grouped by community ID (extracted from candidate metadata `"community_id"`
or `"community"`). Communities smaller than `min_community_size` are filtered out.
Intra-community RRF is computed per community, and communities are ranked by aggregated
relevance before selecting the top nodes up to `max_community_nodes`.
If no community assignments are present in candidate metadata (empty community index),
this method degrades controlledly with `RankError::InvalidInput`.

public_items.name: modulate_and_renormalize_weights
public_items.signature: pub fn modulate_and_renormalize_weights( result_sets: &[(String, Vec<SearchResult>, f32)], calibration_contexts: Option<&[SignalCalibrationContext]>, beta: f32, ) -> Vec<f32>
doc: Modulates signal weights using mRRF margin formula:
$m_s = S_1 - S_2$ (when signal is calibrated AND `drift_status` is `Stable` and $\ge 2$ candidates exist).
$w_s' = w_s \times (1 + g(\beta \times m_s))$.
Renormalizes modulated weights to maintain sum equal to original weight sum (preserving weight norm in [0.999, 1.001]).
Moduliert Signalgewichte anhand der Margin-Differenz (mRRF) und renormalisiert sie.

doc: Bounded smooth influence function $g(x) = \frac{x}{1 + |x|}$.
Returns $x / (1 + |x|)$, bounded in $(-1.0, 1.0)$ for all finite $x$.
Returns `0.0` if $x$ is non-finite (`NaN` or `Infinity`).

public_items.name: rrf_fuse
public_items.signature: pub fn rrf_fuse(ranked_lists: &[Vec<ScoredItem>], k: usize) -> Result<Vec<ScoredItem>>
doc: Standard RRF-Fusion gemäß Klassenvertrag RANK-1:
`rrf_fuse(ranked_lists: &[Vec<ScoredItem>], k: usize) -> Result<Vec<ScoredItem>>`.
Berechnet:
$\text{score}(d) = \sum_{l} \frac{1}{k + \text{rank}_l(d)}$
mit 1-basiertem Rang.
# Fehler
Gibt `RankError::InvalidInput` zurück, wenn $k < 1$ ist oder ein Score $\text{NaN}$ / unendlich ist.

public_items.name: reciprocal_rank
public_items.signature: pub fn reciprocal_rank<'a, I>(ranked_ids: &[I], relevant_ids: &AHashSet<&str>) -> f32 where I: AsRef<str> + 'a,
doc: Berechnet den Reciprocal Rank (RR) für eine geordnete Liste von Treffer-IDs.
Findet die 1-basierte Rangposition des ersten relevanten Dokuments und liefert `1.0 / rank`.
Falls kein relevantes Dokument enthalten ist oder die Ergebnisliste leer ist, wird `0.0` zurückgegeben.
# Argumente
* `ranked_ids` - Nach Relevanz absteigend sortierte Dokument-IDs.
* `relevant_ids` - Menge der als relevant geltenden Dokument-IDs.

public_items.name: mean_reciprocal_rank
public_items.signature: pub fn mean_reciprocal_rank<'a, I>(queries: &[(&[I], &AHashSet<&str>)]) -> f32 where I: AsRef<str> + 'a,
doc: Berechnet den Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) über mehrere Abfragen hinweg.
Liefert das arithmetische Mittel der Reciprocal Ranks aller Abfragen.
Bei einer leeren Menge an Abfragen wird `0.0` zurückgegeben.

public_items.name: precision_at_k
public_items.signature: pub fn precision_at_k<'a, I>(ranked_ids: &[I], relevant_ids: &AHashSet<&str>, k: usize) -> f32 where I: AsRef<str> + 'a,
doc: Berechnet Precision@k (Genauigkeit der Top-k-Ergebnisse).
Anteil der relevanten Dokumente unter den ersten `k` Treffern:
`|relevant ∩ top_k| / k`.
Falls `k == 0` oder `ranked_ids.is_empty()`, wird `0.0` zurückgegeben.

public_items.name: recall_at_k
public_items.signature: pub fn recall_at_k<'a, I>(ranked_ids: &[I], relevant_ids: &AHashSet<&str>, k: usize) -> f32 where I: AsRef<str> + 'a,
doc: Berechnet Recall@k (Trefferquote bezogen auf alle bekannten relevanten Dokumente).
Anteil der gefundenen relevanten Dokumente unter den ersten `k` Treffern:
`|relevant ∩ top_k| / |relevant|`.
Falls `k == 0`, `ranked_ids.is_empty()` oder `relevant_ids.is_empty()`, wird `0.0` zurückgegeben.

public_items.name: ndcg_at_k
public_items.signature: pub fn ndcg_at_k<'a, I>(ranked_ids: &[I], relevance_scores: &AHashMap<&str, f32>, k: usize) -> f32 where I: AsRef<str> + 'a,
doc: Berechnet den Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (nDCG@k).
Setzt den tatsächlichen DCG@k ins Verhältnis zum idealen DCG@k (IDCG@k) bei perfekter Sortierung.
Liefert einen normalisierten Wert zwischen `0.0` und `1.0`.
Falls kein relevantes Dokument existiert (IDCG == 0), wird `0.0` zurückgegeben.
# Argumente
* `ranked_ids` - Erhaltene Reihenfolge der Dokument-IDs.
* `relevance_scores` - Relevanz-Grade der Dokumente (z. B. 0.0 bis 4.0 oder Wahrscheinlichkeiten).
* `k` - Maximale Auswertungstiefe.

public_items.name: apply_temporal_validity_filter
public_items.signature: pub fn apply_temporal_validity_filter( results: Vec<crate::fusion::SearchResult>, current_tx: TxId, query_timestamp: Option<u64>, ) -> Vec<crate::fusion::SearchResult>
doc: Applies bi-temporal validity filtering to candidates post-RRF fusion.
Filters out candidate results that are invalid relative to the current transaction `current_tx`
or business timestamp `query_timestamp`.
Candidates without validity window metadata (legacy data) are retained (Fail-Open).

public_items.name: apply_temporal_validity_filter_at
public_items.signature: pub fn apply_temporal_validity_filter_at( results: Vec<crate::fusion::SearchResult>, as_of_timestamp: u64, ) -> Vec<crate::fusion::SearchResult>
doc: Applies historical "as-of" bi-temporal validity filtering to candidates post-RRF fusion.
Evaluates candidate validity at historical point-in-time `as_of_timestamp` (analogous to Graphitis Episode-Pinning).
A candidate is retained ONLY IF `as_of_timestamp` lies within `[valid_from, valid_until)` AND
transaction validity (`tx_valid_to`, ADR-033) is active at that historical timestamp.
Candidates without validity window metadata (legacy data) are retained (Fail-Open for backward compatibility).
